global_consequence_classification.scope: All-order O_A(Y / (log Y)^A) control of ||r_{sm,T}||_Y^2 / (log Y)^4 established via Selberg PNT + C_{chi,var} (TC-059), refined in TC-060/TC-060R by decomposing R(d) = M_{sq,2}(d) + R_{osc}(d) into the residue-defined z = 1/2 drift model M_{sq,2}(d) and the exact residual R_{osc}(d).

Forward Abelian/continuation implication proved analytically outside Lean: if |R_{osc}(d)| = O(d^{1-delta}) for some delta in (0, 1/2], then on Re(z) > 1 - delta >= 1/2 both sum_{d>=1} delta_{sq,2}(d)*d^{-z} and sum_{d>=1} R_{osc}(d)*(d^{-z} - (d+1)^{-z}) converge absolutely and locally uniformly, extending D_lambda''(z)/D_lambda(z) - c_lambda*zeta(z) holomorphically to Re(z) > 1 - delta and ruling out zeros rho_0 of zeta(z) there (where Re(2*rho_0) > 1 => zeta(2*rho_0) != 0 would leave an uncancelled double pole m_{rho_0}*(m_{rho_0}+1)/(z - rho_0)^2). No exact-boundary converse is claimed from local poles alone.

Proved analytically outside Lean using TC-060 Theorem 5's discrete Abel identity, increment bound |delta_{sq,2}(d)| <= 12*log(d+1)/sqrt(d), and finite weighted small-divisor inequality together with TC-057 Theorem 25 (first main conjunct, third item) cutoff lower bounds, inherited TC-059R Theorem 7's smooth-increment window norm estimate, and TC-057R's PNT bound |R_{osc}(d)| <= C_{osc}*d: for every eps > 0, R >= 2, and 2 <= Y <= R, ||r_{sm,T(Y)}^{drift}/(log X)^2||_Y^2 <= (B_{drift}(eps)/(log Y)^4)*G_eps(R)*Y^eps + C_{drift}(eps) and ||r_{sm,<=min(D_0,T-1)}^{osc}/(log X)^2||_Y^2 <= O((log Y)^{-kappa})*G_eps(R)*Y^eps + C_{small}(eps).

SUBGATE-TC-043A remains OPEN and rh_proved remains False: closing E(Y) = O_eps(Y^eps) via Theorem 6 requires controlling the full signed open quantity 8*X_tilde(Y) + 4*||D_{2,core,T(Y)}||_Y^2, where D_{2,core,T(Y)}(X) = (sum_{min(D_0(Y), T(Y)-1) < d <= T(Y)-1} R_{osc}(d)*Delta_d^{sm}(X) - Q_{lambda,T(Y)}^{[2]}(X)) / (log X)^2 retains ALL d up to T(Y) - 1 (including d >= ceil(tau*Y), because Lemma B2's O(Y*(log Y)^{-4}*exp(-2*c_W*sqrt(log Y))) bound is only an absolute upper bound whose majorant divided by Y^eps grows without bound for fixed 0 < eps < 1).
